\code{table.} works on a table from \code{sdata.table(...)}; \code{chart.} on a chart from
\code{table.start\_chart()} or \code{sdata.chart(...)}; \code{numbers.} on numbers from \code{sdata.number\_list(...)}.
The small grey line under a command names its options. For the full story of a command, use
\code{sdata.help("word")}, the \href{https://github.com/bioforkgithub/simplydata/blob/main/docs/manual/simplydata_manual.pdf}{manual} or the \href{https://github.com/bioforkgithub/simplydata/blob/main/docs/manual/simplydataDictionary.pdf}{dictionary}. These cards are
made from simplydata's own code by \code{docs/make\_cheat\_sheet.py}, so they always match the version above.\par}

\card{Start, show and save}{1}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}chart(sdata.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}example(\textquotedbl{}marks\textquotedbl{}))}\opts{\code{data=}, \code{sheet=}, \code{fast=}}}{Start a chart.}{seaborn \code{scatterplot()}}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}example(\textquotedbl{}marks\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{name=}, \code{from\_\allowbreak{}r\_\allowbreak{}package=}}}{A small table to practise with.}{pandas \code{files()}}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}show()}}{Show the chart in a window.}{matplotlib \code{barplot()}, \code{show()}}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}save(\textquotedbl{}marks.\allowbreak{}png\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{file\_\allowbreak{}name}, \code{quality=}, \code{resolution=}, \code{dpi=}, \code{see\_\allowbreak{}through=}}}{Save the chart.}{matplotlib \code{barplot()}, \code{savefig()}, \code{path.\allowbreak{}join()}, \code{gettempdir()}}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}drawn()}}{A table of the numbers the chart drew.}{matplotlib \code{scatter()}, \code{collections.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}offsets()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}text\_\allowbreak{}drawn()}}{A table of every piece of text the chart drew.}{matplotlib \code{scatterplot()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{get\_\allowbreak{}text()}, \code{get\_\allowbreak{}legend().\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}texts()}}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}scales\_\allowbreak{}drawn()}}{A table of the scales the chart drew: x, y and colour.}{matplotlib \code{scatter()}, \code{get\_\allowbreak{}xlim()}, \code{get\_\allowbreak{}ylim()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}size(unit=\textquotedbl{}cm\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{unit=}}}{The size of the saved chart as (width, height).}{matplotlib \code{figure()}, \code{BytesIO()}, \code{savefig()}, \code{open()}, \code{round()}}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}undo()}}{Take the last step back.}{simplydata's own: a chart is a list of steps drawn only when it is shown or saved, so undo takes the last word's steps and settings back before anything is drawn again. In matplotlib you would draw the chart again without that line.}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}matplotlib()}}{Give back the chart as a plain matplotlib Figure, for matplotlib code.}{matplotlib \code{scatterplot()}, \code{annotate()}}

\end{cardtable}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}undo()}}{Take the last step back.}{simplydata's own: it keeps the table as it was before each step and puts back the last one. In pandas or Polars you keep a copy yourself before a step (before = \code{df.\allowbreak{}copy()}) and go back to it.}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}steps()}}{List every step you did to this table, in order.}{simplydata's own: it writes down each step as you do it and lists them. pandas and Polars keep no list of steps; your script is the record.}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}again()}}{Go back to the table as it was at the start.}{simplydata's own: it keeps the table it started with and puts it back, as one more step that \code{undo()} can take back. In pandas or Polars you keep the first table yourself (start = \code{df.\allowbreak{}copy()}) and go back to it.}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}polars()}}{Give back the table as a plain Polars table, for other Python tools.}{pandas \code{read\_\allowbreak{}csv()}, \code{from\_\allowbreak{}pandas()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}multiply\_\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}matrix\_\allowbreak{}by(other\_\allowbreak{}grid)}\opts{\code{other=}, \code{from\_\allowbreak{}the\_\allowbreak{}left=}}}{Multiply the grid by another as matrices: rows times columns.}{NumPy \code{matmul()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}size(kind=\textquotedbl{}biggest stretch\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{kind=}}}{The size of the numbers as one number (a norm). size = \code{numbers.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}size()}}{NumPy \code{linalg.\allowbreak{}matrix\_\allowbreak{}norm()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}distance\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}nearest(is\_\allowbreak{}above=0)}\opts{\code{is\_\allowbreak{}above=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}below=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}least=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}most=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}equal\_\allowbreak{}to=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}not\_\allowbreak{}equal\_\allowbreak{}to=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}between=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}one\_\allowbreak{}of=}, \code{test\_\allowbreak{}method=}, \code{cell\_\allowbreak{}size=}}}{For each cell, the distance to the nearest cell that meets a condition (a distance map).}{SciPy \code{distance\_\allowbreak{}transform\_\allowbreak{}edt()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}move\_\allowbreak{}and\_\allowbreak{}stretch\_\allowbreak{}by(matrix=[[1,\allowbreak{} 0.\allowbreak{}5],\allowbreak{} [0,\allowbreak{} 1]])}\opts{\code{matrix=}, \code{shift=}, \code{formulas=}, \code{test\_\allowbreak{}method=}}}{Move, stretch, shear or turn a grid as a picture, cell by cell from where each new cell comes.}{SciPy \code{affine\_\allowbreak{}transform()}}

\card{Numbers: undo and finish}{56}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}undo()}}{Take the last step back.}{simplydata's own: it keeps the numbers as they were before each step (up to 30 steps) and puts back the last one. With NumPy you keep a copy yourself before a step (before = \code{values.\allowbreak{}copy()}).}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}steps()}}{List every step you did, in order.}{simplydata's own: it writes down each step as you do it and lists them. A NumPy array keeps no list of steps; your script is the record.}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}again()}}{Go back to the numbers as they were at the start.}{simplydata's own: it keeps the numbers you started with and puts them back, as one more step that \code{undo()} can take back. With NumPy you keep the first array yourself.}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}turn\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}table(name=\textquotedbl{}marks\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{name=}}}{Turn the numbers into a simplydata table.}{pandas \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}chart()}}{Start a chart from these numbers.}{seaborn \code{DataFrame()}, \code{histplot()}}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}save(\textquotedbl{}numbers.\allowbreak{}csv\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{file\_\allowbreak{}name}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}step=}, \code{bits=}}}{Save the numbers; the end of the file name decides the type.}{pandas \code{TemporaryDirectory()}, \code{DataFrame().\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}csv()}, \code{path.\allowbreak{}join()}}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}numpy()}}{Give back the numbers as a plain NumPy array, for other Python tools.}{NumPy \code{copy()}}

\end{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}check\_\allowbreak{}if\_\allowbreak{}any\_\allowbreak{}number(is\_\allowbreak{}above=30)}\opts{\code{is\_\allowbreak{}above=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}below=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}least=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}most=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}equal\_\allowbreak{}to=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}not\_\allowbreak{}equal\_\allowbreak{}to=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}between=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}one\_\allowbreak{}of=}, \code{over=}}}{Check whether at least one number passes a test: it says so and gives back True or False.}{NumPy \code{bool()}, \code{any()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}remove\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}where(column=1,\allowbreak{} is\_\allowbreak{}empty=True)}\opts{\code{column=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}above=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}below=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}least=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}most=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}equal\_\allowbreak{}to=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}not\_\allowbreak{}equal\_\allowbreak{}to=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}between=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}one\_\allowbreak{}of=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}empty=}}}{Remove the rows whose number in one column passes a test.}{NumPy \code{array()}}

\cmd{\code{block.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}from(other,\allowbreak{} over=\textquotedbl{}hour\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{other=}, \code{over=}, \code{only\_\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}new\_\allowbreak{}shape=}}}{Add another block's numbers at the end of one direction (NumPy concatenate).}{NumPy \code{arange().\allowbreak{}reshape()}, \code{concatenate()}}

\cmd{\code{block.\allowbreak{}split\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}pieces(3,\allowbreak{} over=\textquotedbl{}hour\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{over=}, \code{only\_\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}new\_\allowbreak{}shape=}}}{Split the block into pieces along a direction; gives back a list of new blocks (NumPy \code{array\_\allowbreak{}split}).}{NumPy \code{arange().\allowbreak{}reshape()}, \code{array\_\allowbreak{}split()}}

\cmd{\code{block.\allowbreak{}split\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}one\_\allowbreak{}block\_\allowbreak{}per(\textquotedbl{}hour\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{direction=}}}{One new block for each position of a direction, without that direction (NumPy unstack).}{NumPy \code{arange().\allowbreak{}reshape()}, \code{unstack()}}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}stack\_\allowbreak{}up([a,\allowbreak{} b,\allowbreak{} c],\allowbreak{} as\_\allowbreak{}new\_\allowbreak{}direction=\textquotedbl{}image\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{blocks=}, \code{as\_\allowbreak{}new\_\allowbreak{}direction=}, \code{only\_\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}new\_\allowbreak{}shape=}}}{Stack blocks of the same shape into one, along a new first direction (NumPy stack).}{NumPy \code{stack()}}

\card{Waves and systems}{65}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}convolve\_\allowbreak{}with([1,\allowbreak{} 2,\allowbreak{} 1])}\opts{\code{other}, \code{keep=}}}{Convolve the numbers with other numbers: each result is a sum of products as one list slides along.}{SciPy \code{convolve()}}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}deconvolve\_\allowbreak{}by([1,\allowbreak{} 2,\allowbreak{} 3])}\opts{\code{other}}}{Undo a convolution: the numbers divided by other numbers (polynomial division).}{SciPy \code{deconvolve()}}

\cmd{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}change\_\allowbreak{}time\_\allowbreak{}step(to=0.\allowbreak{}01,\allowbreak{} time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}001)}\opts{\code{to=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}step=}, \code{test\_\allowbreak{}method=}, \code{sampling\_\allowbreak{}rate=}, \code{fs=}}}{Change the time between readings (resample): fewer readings (with a filter first) or more.}{SciPy \code{round()}, \code{resample()}}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}wave(\textquotedbl{}sine\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} frequency=5,\allowbreak{} time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}01,\allowbreak{} how\_\allowbreak{}many=100)}\opts{\code{shape=}, \code{frequency=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}step=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{high\_\allowbreak{}share=}, \code{rising\_\allowbreak{}share=}, \code{sweep=}, \code{bandwidth=}, \code{at=}, \code{sampling\_\allowbreak{}rate=} and 1 more}}{Numbers that make a wave: a sine, square, sawtooth, chirp, pulse or impulse.}{SciPy \code{arange()}, \code{square()}}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}window\_\allowbreak{}shape(\textquotedbl{}hann\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} how\_\allowbreak{}many=64)}\opts{\code{name=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{periodic=}}}{The weights of a window (taper), such as \code{\textquotedbl{}hann\textquotedbl{}}: high in the middle, low at the ends.}{SciPy \code{get\_\allowbreak{}window()}}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}system(\textquotedbl{}1 / (s**2 + 2*s + 5)\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{formula=}, \code{numerator=}, \code{denominator=}, \code{poles=}, \code{zeros=}, \code{gain=}, \code{a=}, \code{b=}, \code{c=}, \code{d=} and 10 more}}{A linear system (one input, one output) from its formula, coefficients, poles or matrices.}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}step\_\allowbreak{}response(until=10)}\opts{\code{until=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}points=}}}{How the output answers an input that jumps from 0 to 1 and stays there.}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{step()}, \code{linspace()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}impulse\_\allowbreak{}response(until=10)}\opts{\code{until=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}points=}}}{How the output answers a short kick at time 0 (an impulse of size 1).}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{impulse()}, \code{linspace()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}response\_\allowbreak{}to(sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}wave(\textquotedbl{}square\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} frequency=0.\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{} time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}05,\allowbreak{} how\_\allowbreak{}many=400))}\opts{\code{inputs=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}points=}}}{How the output answers any input you give: a simulation.}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{arange()}, \code{square()}, \code{lsim()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}frequency\_\allowbreak{}response(between=[0.\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} 100])}\opts{\code{between=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{unit=}, \code{with\_\allowbreak{}delay=}}}{How much the system passes each frequency (gain) and how much it delays it (phase): the Bode data.}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{freqresp()}, \code{logspace()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{abs()}, \code{log10()}, \code{degrees()}, \code{unwrap()}, \code{angle()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}poles()}}{The poles: the values of s (or z) where the bottom of the formula is 0. They set how it moves.}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{abs()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}zeros()}}{The zeros: the values of s (or z) where the top of the formula is 0 (inputs that do not get through).}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{abs()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}is\_\allowbreak{}stable()}}{True when every response to a bounded input stays bounded (and settles).}{SciPy \code{bool()}, \code{all()}, \code{lti()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}steady\_\allowbreak{}gain()}}{Where the output settles for a constant input of 1 (the DC gain).}{NumPy \code{polyval()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}in\_\allowbreak{}steps(time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}1)}\opts{\code{time\_\allowbreak{}step=}, \code{test\_\allowbreak{}method=}}}{The same system in steps of \code{time\_\allowbreak{}step} (discrete time), for a computer that reads and acts in steps.}{SciPy \code{cont2discrete()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{ravel()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}then(sdata.\allowbreak{}system(\textquotedbl{}1 / s\textquotedbl{}))}\opts{\code{other}}}{This system, then another one after it (in series): the output of this one feeds the other.}{NumPy \code{polymul()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}add(sdata.\allowbreak{}system(\textquotedbl{}1 / (s + 3)\textquotedbl{}))}\opts{\code{other}}}{This system and another side by side, their outputs added (in parallel): both get the same input.}{NumPy \code{polyadd()}, \code{polymul()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}with\_\allowbreak{}feedback()}\opts{\code{through=}, \code{sign=}}}{The closed loop: the output is fed back (through a sensor, say) and taken from the input.}{NumPy \code{polymul()}, \code{polyadd()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}table()}\opts{\code{form=}}}{The system as numbers: \code{form=\textquotedbl{}transfer function\textquotedbl{}} (the coefficients of the top and the bottom, highest power first: power of s (power of z in steps), numerator, denominator), \code{\textquotedbl{}state space\textquotedbl{}} (the matrices A, B, C, D in controller form: matrix, row, column, value; SciPy tf2ss, as R control::tf2ss), \code{\textquotedbl{}poles and zeros\textquotedbl{}} (kind, real part, imaginary part; the last row is the gain), \code{\textquotedbl{}sections\textquotedbl{}} (second-order sections, one row each: numerator 1 to 3 and denominator 1 to 3, highest power first, as SciPy's sos rows; SciPy tf2sos, or the filter's own sections, as R gsignal::tf2sos) or \code{\textquotedbl{}partial fractions\textquotedbl{}} (the formula as a sum of residue / (s - pole) terms, plus any direct terms: SciPy residue, residuez in steps, as R gsignal::residue and residuez).}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{concatenate()}, \code{zeros()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}chart()}\opts{\code{show=}, \code{between=}, \code{until=}, \code{unit=}}}{A chart of the system: \code{show=\textquotedbl{}bode\textquotedbl{}} (gain in decibels and phase against frequency on a log scale, two panels; \code{\textquotedbl{}gain and phase\textquotedbl{}} is accepted), \code{\textquotedbl{}step\textquotedbl{}}, \code{\textquotedbl{}impulse\textquotedbl{}}, \code{\textquotedbl{}poles and zeros\textquotedbl{}} (x for poles, o for zeros; the unit circle for a system in steps; \code{\textquotedbl{}pole-zero\textquotedbl{}} is accepted) or \code{\textquotedbl{}nyquist\textquotedbl{}} (the frequency response as one curve; a feedback loop is stable when it stays clear of -1).}{matplotlib \code{lti()}, \code{freqresp()}, \code{findfreqs()}, \code{plot()}, \code{log10()}, \code{abs()}, \code{set\_\allowbreak{}ylabel()}, \code{degrees()}, \code{unwrap()}, \code{angle()}, \code{set\_\allowbreak{}xscale()}, \code{set\_\allowbreak{}xlabel()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}move\_\allowbreak{}poles\_\allowbreak{}to([-2,\allowbreak{} -3])}\opts{\code{to=}}}{The system with its poles moved to new places by feeding back its inner state (pole placement).}{SciPy \code{tf2ss()}, \code{place\_\allowbreak{}poles()}, \code{ss2tf()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{ravel()}}

\end{cardtable}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}all\_\allowbreak{}words()}}{Print every simplydata word with a short example.}{simplydata's own: it prints its own word list, group by group, with a short example of each.}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}help(\textquotedbl{}draw\_\allowbreak{}bars\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{word=}}}{Explain one word: what it does, its options and an example you can run.}{simplydata's own: it reads its own word list and the words' docstrings, in plain Python. Python's \code{help()} shows a function's docstring too.}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}lesson(1)}\opts{\code{number=}, \code{solutions=}}}{A lesson: an example to run, what each line does, and a task.}{simplydata's own: the lessons are written in simplydata (learn.py) and printed in plain Python; nothing is computed.}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}packages\_\allowbreak{}used()}\opts{\code{save\_\allowbreak{}as=}, \code{at\_\allowbreak{}end=}}}{List the packages that did the work behind your simplydata words, and how to cite them.}{simplydata's own: it notes which packages its words called, reads their versions from the installed metadata (Python's importlib.metadata; R's \code{packageVersion()} and \code{citation()} through rpy2 for R packages) and prints each reference with a sentence for your methods. No data are worked on; \code{importlib.\allowbreak{}metadata.\allowbreak{}version(\textquotedbl{}pandas\textquotedbl{})} gives one version yourself.}

\end{cardtable}
